correctness.rationale: A finite irreducible CTMC has unique spin-inversion-symmetric stationarity. Exact generator second-moment equations reduce to three correlation values; the cross-part equation correctly includes direct partner copying. Solving gives u=v=s/(s+2mu(2+mu)), w=(1+mu)u. Summing the ordered pairs gives the rational variance. Strict derivative in P=ab establishes fixed-size extremizers. With H=ab/(a+b), variance=(1+2mu(3+mu)H/N)/(1+2mu(2+mu)H), H comparable to min(a,b) and H/N≤1/4, giving the iff self-averaging criterion and fixed-core positive limit. Standard-library verifier independently solved 48 finite exact stationary master equations and 714 rational assertions. No finite check is used as proof of infinite claims.

value.rationale: The precise stationary fluctuation cutoff is motivated by whether global opinion fluctuations average away in enlarging heterogeneous interaction networks. The result gives an iff criterion based on the smaller partition rather than population size, distinguishes all fixed-size optimal architectures, and yields an unexpected positive fluctuation floor when one partition stays bounded even as N diverges. Exact opposite-side versus same-side correlations explain the mechanism and make the formula usable as a finite-network benchmark for noisy-voter approximations. These are intrinsic all-size structural statements rather than an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
